misreadings.quote: now a cell locked from the outside by his "beneficiaries."
misreadings.evidence: "now that he had opened up one of the doors and the other had clearly been unlocked some time during the day, no-one came, and the keys were in the other sides."
misreadings.explanation: The text says one door was opened by Gregor and the other was unlocked, so it does not show that the family locked him in from the outside.

misreadings.quote: the very people who have now moved the keys to the outside of his door
misreadings.evidence: "the keys were in the other sides."
misreadings.explanation: The text only says the keys were on the other sides; it does not say the family moved them or why.

misreadings.quote: yet his body finds relief in the pressure against his back
misreadings.evidence: "he hurried under the couch. It pressed down on his back a little, and he was no longer able to li"
misreadings.explanation: The text says the couch pressed on his back but, as far as it was read, never says this brought relief (the translation's "deep relief" goes further still).

misreadings.quote: his new biology finds it repulsive
misreadings.evidence: "the pain in his tender left side make it difficult to eat the food... but the milk did not taste at all nice."
misreadings.explanation: The milk simply did not taste nice and eating hurt; the text does not say he found it repulsive.

result.note: Most of the reflection is interpretation; the errors are the claim that Gregor is locked in from the outside with the keys moved by the family, and the unsupported relief under the couch.
